content:
Although Apple's revamped personal assistant is undoubtedly the headline feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate, this year's update also includes many other new features and improvements unrelated to Siri AI. After checking out my carefully selected favourite new features of macOS 27, don't forget to watch my video where I'll demonstrate each one for you.

Major App Icon Overhaul

macOS 27 has changed virtually every built-in app icon to some degree, with the icons for Siri, Preview, and Chess receiving complete redesigns. Other app icons, such as Finder, Photos, and Reminders, have received noticeable revamps that lean into the Liquid Glass design language. In macOS Golden Gate, almost no app icon escapes change, though many updates are quite subtle.

If you watch my video below, you'll see a slider comparison showing what each app icon looked like in macOS Tahoe alongside its new appearance in macOS Golden Gate.

Some updates, like the Photos app icon, I quite like. Others, like Finder, I haven't fully come around on yet. Let me know what you think of these app icon changes in the comments below.

Video: macOS 27 Top Features and Changes

Full HDR Support

One of the best things about macOS 27 is its full HDR support for OS-level visual effects. Icons, toolbars, and other parts of the Liquid Glass design language have gained support for additional dynamic range, something users with HDR-capable displays will notice immediately.

To identify which elements have additional dynamic range, you can use macOS's built-in Digital Color Meter tool to watch for clipping in shadows or highlights while viewing native SDR values. Be sure to watch my video where I'll explore different parts of the OS to demonstrate HDR support.

If you're a Studio Display XDR user, you've definitely already noticed the difference, but even if you can't afford Apple's most expensive display, you can still enjoy these benefits on third-party HDR-capable displays.

I recently got hands-on with Asus's ProArt QD-OLED 32-inch 4K display, and thanks to its panel technology, HDR looks fantastic across the OS. Unlike Apple's own displays with Extended Dynamic Range support, you'll need to head to Settings > Displays and flip the High Dynamic Range toggle to enjoy these benefits.

Recently, I've started using the Dell UltraSharp U3226Q QD-OLED display, which I'm really loving — a review is coming soon. On both displays, HDR elements really pop, like the shimmering cursor in the newly designed Spotlight/Siri AI interface.

Design Updates

macOS Golden Gate is packed with design updates aimed at addressing user complaints about macOS Tahoe. One of my biggest complaints was the inconsistent corner radius on some windows.

Of course, that wasn't the only complaint addressed, but it's the most important one to me. Other fixes include floating sidebars being reverted to edge-to-edge sidebars, improved toolbars with prominent dividers, and the Liquid Glass effect itself has been refined, including a new slider that lets users fine-tune the balance between transparency and tinting.

Streamlined Menus

Another major complaint about macOS Tahoe was how much unnecessary clutter piled up in menus. In macOS Tahoe, nearly every menu option had a corresponding icon symbol, making menus look visually messy.

If every menu item has an icon, you eventually run out of reasonable icon options while reducing the usefulness of the original icons. I'm glad Apple fixed this.

iPhone Mirroring

iPhone Mirroring on macOS 27 gets three major improvements that make the feature much more useful on Golden Gate.

  • You can now access Control Center from the mirrored iPhone.
  • You can resize the iPhone Mirroring window to more closely match the aspect ratio of an iPad mini.
  • You can play DRM-protected content from your iPhone on your Mac without getting a black screen.

Without question, iPhone Mirroring is far more useful in macOS 27!

9to5Mac's Take

While Siri AI has dominated most of the headlines, macOS Golden Gate is about more than just Siri. I've highlighted some of my favourite new features in this article, but there's plenty more to explore. Watch my full video for a look at all the new features, and let me know your favourites in the comments.
